00 · Baseline — ProtoPie recreation

Stylist copy, orbiting products, snap-to-full reveal

Faithful to the recording: the confirmed photo shrinks into a centered card while seven lines of stylist copy rotate under a spinner. At 8s the raw photo crossfades to the background-removed cut-out on the grey card and the three products drift slowly around it below the shoulder line (the Rotate3d “Omni” layer), never crossing the face. At 16s the chips collapse, the card dips, then snaps out to full-bleed on the final render and “Shop this look” rises.

Every image is shown exactly as delivered — the only things animating are containers, opacity and copy.

A · Fitting Room

A ticket that fills in, and a mirror that turns

The wait is reframed as a fitting: a hairline progress rule under the card counts the first 8s while the copy says what the backend is actually doing. When the cut-out arrives the card flips like a mirror turning (the cut-out is the card’s back face — no image is touched). The three products sit in a ticket below and light up one at a time across the second 8s, each with its own line of copy, so the user reads the wait as three small steps rather than one long one. The final render arrives with a second flip, and the ticket becomes “Shop this look”.

B · Contact Sheet

One tall frame, a wipe, and a darkroom timer

Editorial and quiet: the photo becomes a tall 4:5 frame with the three products in a thin contact-sheet strip at its right edge, labelled by slot. A single hairline scans down the photo during background removal; when the cut-out lands it is revealed by a top-to-bottom wipe (a clip-path on the new layer over the old one — pixels untouched). Products in the strip come alive as the second stage runs, and the final render wipes down the same way before the frame expands to full-bleed. A tabular-number timer at the foot gives the wait a fixed, honest length.
